title: Later Alligator: Sweet Geraldine and character-specific reactions

people.name: Lindsay Small-Butera
people.role: Director; writing, concepting, storyboarding, animation and design (self-described in interview)

people.name: Alex Small-Butera
people.role: Keyframer; animation and design (described by Lindsay in joint interview)

summary: Large directional eyes and a small curved mouth make a boastful dialogue pose legible without a large facial rig.

observations.text: In the inspected Sweet Geraldine frame, huge eyes look upward while the small mouth curves up toward the snout. A fang and tilted face add personality; the pose reads alongside her boast about being a claw-machine mastermind.
Lindsay says the reaction sets were decided case by case around each alligator's conversation nodes, with shared categories including wins, losses, happy, sad, disappointed and angry.
The duo describe getting the feeling of the gesture down rapidly and refining it in later passes. Alex describes exporting labeled PNG sequences from Harmony for assembly in Unity.

mistIdeas: Our inference: give MIST distinct confident, sheepish and uncertain resting mouth shapes before adding movement. The eyes should establish attention, with the mouth providing attitude.
Our inference: author reactions to concrete events such as recognition, misunderstanding and successful completion. Reuse broad emotion categories but choose a different held pose for each event.

title: Slime Rancher: six faces and a separate mouth mask

people.name: Ian McConville
people.role: Principal Artist; author of the Slime Rancher 1.4.0 face-shader rebuild (the post spells the title 'Principle Artist')

summary: A developer-supplied six-face GIF shows how much expression can fit on the same nearly featureless round body.

observations.text: In the inspected GIF frame, the happy bottom-centre face uses dot eyes and a broad open mouth; the worried bottom-right face retains tiny eyes but replaces that mouth with a small downturned shape. The body design stays consistent.
The startled bottom-left face enlarges the eye marks and uses a small open mouth. This is an expression-shape comparison, not a verified timing analysis.

McConville describes separate eye and mouth channels in an RGBA distance-field mask, mouth-size changes through smoothstep, and UV noise for face wobble. He says swapping the source texture produces different faces.

mistIdeas: Our inference: keep MIST's familiar eyes and body, and author a small set of clearly different mouth silhouettes before adding more continuous movement.

Our inference: separate gaze, eye aperture, and mouth state so a listening response can move the eyes first and change the mouth only after recognition. The delayed timing is our proposal, not a measured property of this GIF.
Our inference: use wobble as a small secondary effect; it should not replace authored reactions or make every state equally active.

title: Dicey Dungeons: Lady Luck and the newly transformed warrior
studio: Terry Cavanagh, Marlowe Dobbe and Chipzel
summary: An official dialogue GIF gives a clear comparison between composed, knowing attention and open excitement in the same scene.

observations.text: In the inspected GIF frame, Lady Luck has a half-lidded sideways eye, a high curved brow and a small angular smile. The warrior has open eyes, raised brows and an open grin. Their attitudes remain distinct at a glance.

The facial contrast is supported by gesture: Lady Luck presents an open palm while the warrior holds his sword up. Only a sampled GIF frame was inspected; this does not establish timing or lip-sync behavior.

mistIdeas: Our inference: build a mildly amused listening pose around eyelid height and sideways gaze, then keep that eye pose while the mouth changes for speech.
Our inference: distinguish alert delight from ordinary warmth with eye opening and brow height before increasing mouth size. Avoid giving every positive state the warrior's excited grin.

title: OMORI: a held face with changing pencil contours

people.name: OMOCAT
people.role: OMORI Game Director, Illustrator, Writer, Programmer, Animator / Video Editor, among other project roles listed in the artist CV; individual GIF authorship is not separately itemized.

summary: The supplied portrait GIF keeps a nearly neutral face while the contours change slightly, showing how a held expression can remain visibly drawn without constant emotional movement.

observations.text: The artist's portfolio GIF has a frontal head, dark oval eyes, gently angled brows and a very small mouth. Across its three decoded frames, the same neutral expression remains while hair, shoulders and contours shift slightly.

The mouth remains tiny relative to the eyes and dark hair mass. The drawing does not need a wide mouth or a smile to read as a face; this is useful when a character is listening or withholding a response.

OMOCAT's portfolio CV explicitly includes animation and video editing among their OMORI roles. It also credits illustration separately, so this is stronger evidence than inferring animation work from a general art credit.

mistIdeas: Our inference: design a readable listening pose with a very small mouth and stable gaze, then allow only a faint surface or contour variation if it suits MIST's existing material.
Our inference: reserve a blink, gaze change or mouth opening for a conversational event. A held emotional pose and visual texture can be controlled independently.
Our inference: do not copy pencil jitter directly onto a robot display without testing. The transferable choice is restrained acting; the handmade texture is optional.

title: Cuphead: Hopus Pocus: mouth shapes that change the character

people.name: Tina Nawrocki
people.role: Animator of Hopus Pocus, identified in her own production post

summary: A small two-tooth smile and a predatory grin feel different while preserving the same rabbit.

observations.text: The first attack drawing has a small mouth and two front teeth beneath narrowed, offset eyelids. Other drawings expose a long serrated grin and larger eye openings.
The smear drawing stretches head and hands together. Nose, eye masses and grin remain grouped rather than moving as unrelated parts.
The death drawing stretches the neck and pulls the eyes into unequal vertical shapes; nose and ears still identify the rabbit.

mistIdeas: Our inference: draw different mouth silhouettes for interest, delight and alarm rather than scaling one oval.
Our inference: test one coordinated facial distortion followed by a return to the neutral layout; these stills do not establish its duration.
